reasoning_summary: Selected features prioritize stable, interpretable credit risk signals with zero missingness and broad semantic coverage. External scores (EXT_SOURCE) lead due to their strong predictive power and stability. Bureau-related debt and credit history aggregates are included as they reflect durable indebtedness and repayment behavior, selecting representative aggregates to control redundancy. Employment and income capacity features are chosen for interpretability and stability. Installment repayment behavior features are included focusing on mean and max aggregates to capture repayment patterns without overloading on redundant variance metrics. Previous application behavior features are selected to provide exposure and capacity signals, favoring those with lower missingness and meaningful credit-risk interpretation. Application amount and demographic features are included to cover customer history and capacity. Credit card utilization features are included selectively, preferring mean and max aggregates with stable coverage. Delinquency and POS cash balance features are included sparingly to add behavioral signals. Redundancy is controlled by selecting representative features within semantic groups, avoiding tail-dominated or sparse variables. All features have zero missingness and are defensible in scorecard reviews.
